name: Ears & air pressure

overlay.caption: cabin air pushes in · air behind the eardrum is trapped · a swallow opens the tube and evens it out

does: Shows the pressure difference building as the cabin pressure rises during the descent
Shows each swallow or yawn letting air through a small tube to even it out (halving it)
Shows why the descent, not the climb, is usually the uncomfortable part
doesnt: Measure any real person or plane — the numbers are illustrative teaching values
Include a blocked nose, which makes the tube harder to open
Model diving, where the pressure changes much faster
limits.text: This is a simplified learning model. Real people vary with age, fitness and health. The numbers are illustrative, not measurements of any real person.
limits.wellbeing: Ear pain that doesn't go away after landing is a reason to tell an adult.

sources: NIH NIDCD: How do we hear? — the middle ear (student overview)
